title: United Arab Emirates | Central Bank Law 2025: Licensing, Conduct, Fraud and Reporting
tagline: The UAE's 2025 Central Bank law in practice: licences and Authorized Individuals, customer protection, fraud, qualified reporting staff and sanctions.
sectors: Conventional banks licensed by the Central Bank of the UAE
Finance companies and other CBUAE-licensed institutions
Compliance, legal and internal audit functions
Retail banking, complaints and fraud prevention teams
description:
A country-specific quest for staff of **onshore conventional banks and other financial institutions licensed by the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE)**. It is built on **Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 Regarding the Central Bank, Regulation of Financial Institutions and Activities, and Insurance Business**, read in full in the English text published by the UAE Ministry of Finance. The law replaced Decretal Federal Law No. 14 of 2018 and does not apply in the financial free zones.

The quest covers the Central Bank's objectives and powers, licensing and Authorized Individuals, governance approvals, customer confidentiality, complaints, the ban on compound interest, fraud prevention, regulatory reporting, examinations, sanctions and the transitional provisions. Its main audience is **regulatory reporting and finance staff**, because Article 122 requires banks to appoint qualified employees to prepare the reports the Central Bank requires; managers, compliance, fraud and customer-facing staff will also benefit. AML/CFT/CPF duties are covered in a separate quest, and the CBUAE Rulebook's detailed regulations are referred to only in general terms.

It builds knowledge and does not replace your institution's own policies and procedures or the Central Bank's current Rulebook.
audience: Regulatory reporting analysts, reviewers and heads of reporting in CBUAE-licensed institutions
Finance and financial reporting teams who prepare year-end packages and disclosures
Compliance, legal and internal audit staff who map the 2025 law to policies and controls
Board members, chief executives and other Authorized Individuals
Retail, complaints and fraud prevention staff who apply the customer protection articles
outcomes: Explain the scope of the 2025 Central Bank law, the Central Bank's objectives and how its rules are made and published
Apply the licensing, Designated Function and prior approval rules to real business decisions
Handle customer data, complaints, interest and fraud cases in line with Articles 147-150
Prepare and defend Central Bank reports as a qualified employee under Article 122
Describe examination powers, sanctions, appeal routes and personal liability, and build a readiness file

cards.title: A new law on the desk
cards.setting: Dunecrest Bank head office, Abu Dhabi. Sunday, 8:15 am.

lines.text: Your first morning in Regulatory Reporting at Dunecrest Bank PJSC, a fictional onshore conventional bank with branches in Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah and Ajman.
Welcome! You have joined in an interesting year. Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 now governs the Central Bank and every licensed financial institution in the country.
I want a gap analysis against the new law for the board. Where do we stand on licensing, customers, fraud, reporting and sanctions?
Quick question first. Half our procedures cite circulars issued under the 2018 law. Are they all dead now?
Not automatically. The new law keeps the old regulations alive until the Central Bank replaces them. But it also gave every institution one year to align.
So stage one is the map: what the law is, who the Central Bank is, what it wants, and how its rules reach your desk.

cards.title: The law that governs your bank

scenes.heading: One law, three topics
scenes.narration: Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 covers the Central Bank, the regulation of financial institutions and activities, and insurance business. It was issued on 8 September 2025 and replaced the 2018 Central Bank law.

scenes.heading: Where it applies
scenes.narration: Article 2 applies the law to the Central Bank, financial institutions, insurance and financial activities in the country. It does not apply to the financial free zones or to the firms their own authorities regulate.

scenes.heading: An independent central bank
scenes.narration: Under Article 3 the Central Bank of the UAE is a federal public institution with financial and managerial independence. It reports directly to the President of the State.

scenes.heading: Three objectives
scenes.narration: Article 5 gives it three aims: keep the national currency stable, help promote and protect the stability of the financial system, and manage the foreign reserves prudently.

scenes.heading: How rules reach you
scenes.narration: The Central Bank issues regulations, standards, circulars and guidelines, and keeps them all in an electronic Rulebook on its website. Licensed institutions must comply with them.

cards.title: How a Central Bank rule reaches your desk
cards.caption: Article numbers are from the Ministry of Finance's English copy of Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025.

items.label: The law sets the powers
items.detail: Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 lets the Central Bank regulate licensed activities and conduct (Article 5).

items.label: Board approves the rule
items.detail: The Central Bank's board approves regulations, standards and licensing conditions (Article 16).

items.label: Optional public consultation
items.detail: The Central Bank may ask the public or industry for views on draft rules within a set period (Article 30).

items.label: Published in the Rulebook
items.detail: All regulations sit in an electronic guide on the Central Bank's website, kept up to date (Article 131).

items.label: Banks must comply
items.detail: Licensed institutions follow all regulations, circulars and instructions (Article 114).

items.label: No retroactive effect
items.detail: New rules do not reach back, and customer agreements signed earlier can still be carried out (Article 132).

cards.question: Which of these is one of the Central Bank's three objectives under Article 5(1) of the 2025 law?
options: Maximising the profits of licensed banks in the country
Setting the federal budget together with the Ministry of Finance
Contributing to the promotion and protection of the financial system's stability
Supervising firms in the financial free zones
cards.explanation: Article 5(1) lists currency stability, contributing to financial system stability, and prudent management of foreign reserves. Bank profits are not an objective, the budget is not its job (it coordinates monetary and fiscal policy under Article 34), and the free zones are outside the law's scope under Article 2.

cards.title: Objectives and functions (Article 5)
cards.body:
**Objectives (Article 5(1))**
- Keep the national currency stable within the monetary system.
- Contribute to promoting and protecting the stability of the financial system.
- Manage the Central Bank's foreign reserves prudently.

**Functions and powers (Article 5(2)), among others**
- Set and carry out monetary policy.
- Regulate licensed financial activities and promote sound conduct and prudent practice, in line with the law and international standards.
- Issue regulations, standards, circulars and guidelines so that licensed activities are run with **integrity, prudence and professional competence**, and not against the interests of customers.
- Foster sustainable finance and build ESG principles into its own work.
- Monitor systemic risk and oversee financial market infrastructures.

Note the words *professional competence*: the law itself expects the people who run licensed activities to know what they are doing.

cards.title: Find the article
cards.prompt: Match each topic to the article of Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 that deals with it.

pairs.right: The law does not apply to the financial free zones or the firms they regulate
The Central Bank is independent and reports directly to the President
An electronic Rulebook holds all Central Bank regulations
Central Bank rules have no retroactive effect
Regulations made under the 2018 law stay in force until replaced
Everyone subject to the law has one year to align, extendable by the board

cards.title: The circular question
cards.setting: Regulatory Reporting floor, Abu Dhabi. 11:00 am.

lines.text: Layla, our large exposures procedure cites a regulation issued under the 2018 law. Do we bin it?
Article 183 says regulations, standards, guidelines and circulars issued under the 2018 law stay in force until the Central Bank issues replacements.
And the definitions in them? Some terms changed in the new law.
The old definitions keep their meaning inside those old regulations until they are replaced. Article 183 covers that too.
But don't relax. Article 184 gave everyone one year from entry into force to bring their position in line with the new law, unless the Central Bank's board extends it.
Then the board wants to see that we did that, article by article.

cards.title: The 'old law' procedure
cards.situation: During the gap analysis you find that Dunecrest's credit policy still quotes the 2018 law as its legal basis, although the underlying Central Bank regulation it applies has not been replaced. A colleague suggests either deleting the policy's legal references entirely or leaving the document untouched.

choices.text: Keep applying the regulation, which stays in force under Article 183, but update the policy's legal basis to the 2025 law and log the change in the gap analysis
choices.outcome: Best answer. The regulation still binds the bank until it is replaced, so the controls stay. The 2018 law has been repealed (Article 185), so the policy should cite the 2025 law, and the gap analysis shows the board how the bank aligned within the Article 184 period.

choices.text: Leave the policy untouched, because old regulations remain valid until replaced
choices.outcome: Partly right. The regulation is still in force, but the policy now cites a repealed law. That weakens the document and suggests the bank has not reviewed it against the new law.

choices.text: Suspend the policy until the Central Bank issues a new credit regulation
choices.outcome: Poor. Suspending controls leaves the bank without a policy while the old regulation still applies. Article 183 exists precisely to avoid a vacuum.

choices.text: Delete every legal reference so the policy never goes out of date
choices.outcome: Poor. Staff and examiners need to see which rule each control implements. Removing references makes the policy harder to audit and does not fix the gap.

cards.title: From the 2018 law to full alignment
cards.caption: Entry-into-force date as recorded in the checked UAE jurisdiction map; the law itself says it applies from the day after publication.

items.label: Previous Central Bank law
items.detail: Decretal Federal Law No. 14 of 2018 governed the Central Bank and financial institutions.

items.label: New decree-law issued
items.detail: Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 is issued in Abu Dhabi.

items.label: In force
items.detail: It applies from the day after Official Gazette publication (Article 188) and repeals the 2018 law (Article 185).

items.label: Alignment period ends
items.detail: Institutions had one year from entry into force to align; the Central Bank's board may extend this (Article 184).

cards.front: Licensed Financial Institution
cards.back: Banks, (re)insurance companies and other financial institutions licensed under the law to carry on one or more licensed financial activities.

cards.front: Bank
cards.back: A legal person licensed mainly to take deposits, plus any other licensed financial activities.

cards.front: Authorized Individual
cards.back: A person the Central Bank has authorized to perform a Designated Function at a licensed institution.

cards.front: Designated Functions
cards.back: Roles with an influential effect on a licensed institution's activities, such as board member or chief executive.

cards.front: Rulebook
cards.back: The Central Bank's electronic guide of all its regulations, published and updated on its website (Article 131).

cards.front: The Dirham (AED)
cards.back: The national currency, divided into 100 fils. Notes and the digital form are legal tender for any amount (Articles 52 and 54).

items.label: Board members
items.detail: Including the Chairman and the Governor (Article 11), appointed for renewable four-year terms (Article 12).

items.label: Board meets at least
items.detail: The board holds an ordinary meeting at least once every sixty days (Article 18).

items.label: Paid-up capital
items.detail: The Central Bank's paid-up capital is twenty billion dirhams (Article 6).

items.label: Minimum reserve cover
items.detail: Foreign reserves must be worth at least 70% of the monetary base (Article 46).

cards.question: A Central Bank regulation issued in 2026 tightens a disclosure rule. A customer agreement signed in 2024 conflicts with it. What does Article 132 say?
options: The regulation has no retroactive effect and does not stop the earlier agreement from being carried out
The 2024 agreement becomes void on the day the regulation is published
The bank must renegotiate every earlier agreement within twenty working days
The customer must sign a new agreement before any further payment is made
cards.explanation: Article 132 says Central Bank rules have no retroactive effect and do not prevent agreements made before them from being implemented. The Central Bank sets any transitional period. Nothing in the article voids or forces renegotiation of earlier contracts.

cards.title: Inside or outside the law's reach?
cards.prompt: Under Articles 2 and 62, which of these fall within Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025?

items.text: Dunecrest Bank's branch network in Sharjah
A finance company licensed by the Central Bank in Ajman
An exchange house offering instant money transfers onshore
An app offering payment services onshore through a decentralized protocol
A firm regulated by the authority of a financial free zone
A bank's branch licensed and supervised inside a financial free zone

cards.title: Dunecrest's gap analysis (fictional)
cards.body:
Noura splits the 2025 law into the parts that bind a bank day to day and gives each an owner:

| Part of the law | Owner at Dunecrest |
|---|---|
| Licensing and scope (Arts 60-73) | Legal and Compliance |
| Authorized Individuals (Arts 107-112) | HR and Company Secretary |
| Supervision and reporting (Arts 120-141) | Regulatory Reporting and Finance |
| Customer protection and fraud (Arts 147-152) | Retail, Fraud Risk and Complaints |
| Sanctions and penalties (Arts 167-181) | Compliance and Legal |

For each article the owner records: what the law requires, which policy or control meets it, any gap, and the fix date. Where the bank relies on a regulation issued under the 2018 law, the file notes that it stays in force under Article 183 until replaced.

The result is a single document the board can approve and an examiner can follow.

cards.title: Stage 1 take-aways
items: Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 governs the Central Bank and licensed financial institutions onshore; it does not apply in the financial free zones (Article 2).
The Central Bank is independent, reports to the President and aims at currency stability, financial stability and prudent reserve management (Articles 3 and 5).
Its rules sit in the electronic Rulebook (Article 131), bind licensed institutions (Article 114) and have no retroactive effect (Article 132).
Regulations made under the 2018 law stay in force until replaced (Article 183), and institutions had one year to align, extendable by the board (Article 184).

cards.prompt: Pick one procedure you use every week. Which article of the 2025 law, or which surviving regulation, does it implement, and does the document say so?

quiz.question: Which law did Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 repeal for the Central Bank and financial institutions?
options: Decretal Federal Law No. 14 of 2018
Federal Decree-Law No. 50 of 2022 on Commercial Transactions
Federal Law No. 8 of 2004 on Financial Free Zones
Federal Decree-Law No. 32 of 2021 on Commercial Companies
quiz.explanation: Article 185 repeals Decretal Federal Law No. 14 of 2018 (and the 2023 insurance law). The free zones law, companies law and commercial transactions law are only cited in the preamble and remain in force.

quiz.question: A firm licensed by the regulator of a financial free zone asks whether Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025 governs its activities there. What does Article 2 say?
options: The law applies only to its retail customers who live onshore
It applies in full, because the law covers every financial firm operating anywhere in the country
The law applies once the Central Bank designates the firm as systemically important
It does not apply in the financial free zones or to firms their authorities regulate
quiz.explanation: Article 2 expressly excludes the financial free zones and the institutions regulated by their authorities. Systemic designation under Article 35 concerns licensed institutions and does not extend the law into the free zones.

quiz.question: To whom does the Central Bank report directly under Article 3?
options: The Cabinet
The Minister of Finance
The President of the State
The Financial Stability Board
quiz.explanation: Article 3(1) says the Central Bank reports directly to the President. It coordinates with the Ministry of Finance on monetary and fiscal policy (Article 34) but does not report to the Minister.

quiz.question: Which wording from Article 5(2)(c) best describes what Central Bank rules aim to secure in licensed activities?
options: Lower operating costs and faster product approvals so that banks can compete regionally
Maximum lending growth and market share for national banks
Uniform pricing of products across all licensed institutions
Integrity, prudence and professional competence, without harming customers
quiz.explanation: Article 5(2)(c) says rules should ensure licensed activities are carried on with integrity, prudence and appropriate professional competence and not against customers' interests. Growth, costs and price uniformity are not stated aims.

quiz.question: Arjun finds a guideline issued under the 2018 law that the Central Bank has not yet replaced. What is its status?
options: It lapsed when the 2018 law was repealed
It applies only if the bank's board readopts it
It remains in force until the Central Bank issues a replacement
It applies only to institutions licensed before 2018
quiz.explanation: Article 183 keeps regulations, decisions, standards, guidelines and circulars issued under the 2018 law in force until replaced. Repeal of the old law under Article 185 does not cancel them, and no board readoption is needed.

quiz.question: How long did institutions have to bring their position in line with the 2025 law, and can that change?
options: One year from entry into force, and the Central Bank's board may extend it
Six months from publication, with no extension possible
Three months from the next inspection, set case by case
Two years from publication in the Official Gazette, extendable only by a Cabinet resolution
quiz.explanation: Article 184 gives one year from the date the law came into force and lets the Central Bank's board extend the period as it sees fit. The other periods do not appear in the law.

quiz.question: Where must the Central Bank publish all the regulations it issues under the law?
options: Only in the Official Gazette, as printed notices
In a confidential manual sent to bank boards
In the annual report it sends to the President
In an electronic guide on its official website, kept regularly updated
quiz.explanation: Article 131 requires an electronic guide (the Rulebook) containing all regulations, published and regularly updated on the Central Bank's website. The Gazette is used for other decisions, and the annual report is a different duty under Article 10.

quiz.question: A product manager says a new Central Bank rule means Dunecrest must stop honouring loan terms agreed last year. Which response is correct?
options: Rules are not retroactive and do not stop earlier agreements being carried out
Rules apply from publication to all existing contracts, so the conflicting old terms become void
The bank may choose case by case whether to honour old terms
Old terms stay valid only if the customer files an objection
quiz.explanation: Article 132 states that regulations, decisions and circulars have no retroactive effect and do not stop agreements made before them from being implemented, with the Central Bank setting any transition period. Customer objections and bank discretion are not part of the rule.

quiz.question: A payments start-up says it is outside the Central Bank's reach because it offers transfers through a decentralized application rather than a bank account. What does Article 62 say?
options: Anyone offering a licensed activity is within the Central Bank's reach, whatever the technology
Decentralized applications are regulated only once they start to hold customer deposits directly
Technology firms fall under the Central Bank only if a bank owns them
Only activities run on traditional banking systems need a Central Bank licence
quiz.explanation: Article 62 brings anyone carrying on, offering or facilitating a licensed financial activity under Central Bank licensing and oversight, regardless of medium or technology, naming DeFi, platforms, dApps and protocols. Deposits and ownership are not conditions.

quiz.question: Which statement about the Central Bank's board is accurate under the 2025 law?
options: It has nine members elected by banks and meets at least quarterly
Seven members including the Chairman and the Governor; it meets at least every sixty days
Five members appointed by the Minister of Finance; it meets at least once a calendar month
It has seven members, none of whom may be the Governor
quiz.explanation: Article 11 sets a seven-member board including the Chairman and the Governor, and Article 18 requires an ordinary meeting at least every sixty days. Members are appointed by federal decree on the Cabinet's recommendation (Article 12), not elected by banks.

sessions.title: Licensing, Authorized Individuals and Prior Approvals
sessions.summary: The ban on unlicensed activity and promotion, the list of licensed financial activities, the licensing path, Designated Functions that need individual authorization, and the changes that need the Central Bank's prior approval.
objectives: Identify licensed financial activities and the bans on unlicensed activity and promotion (Articles 60-62)
Describe the licensing decision periods, the register and the grounds for suspending a licence
Apply the prior authorization rules for Designated Functions and Authorized Individuals (Articles 107-112)
Recognise corporate changes that need prior Central Bank approval

cards.title: The partner and the new CFO
cards.setting: Executive floor, Dunecrest Bank, Abu Dhabi. Tuesday, 9:30 am.

lines.text: Two quick wins for this quarter. A fintech partner will offer instant money transfers under our name, and our new CFO starts on Monday.
Two questions before anything starts. Is the partner itself licensed for that activity? And has the Central Bank authorized the CFO yet?
The CFO's paperwork is with HR. Can't he act as CFO while we wait?
A chief financial officer role is very likely a Designated Function. Under Article 107 nobody performs one without the Central Bank's prior authorization.
And if the partner promotes transfers to our customers without a licence, that is a promotion problem too, not just a licensing one.
Stage two: who may do what. Licences for institutions, authorizations for people, and the approvals the board must get first.

scenes.heading: The basic ban
scenes.narration: Article 60 says nobody may carry on a licensed financial activity without a Central Bank licence, and nobody may present themselves as a licensed institution if they are not one.

scenes.heading: Promotion counts too
scenes.narration: Promoting a licensed activity or financial product is allowed only as the law and its rules permit. Promotion means any communication that invites someone to enter a transaction or agreement for a licensed activity.

scenes.heading: The activities list
scenes.narration: Article 61 lists the licensed activities, including taking deposits, credit facilities, open finance, currency exchange and money transfer, stored value and digital money, payment services using virtual assets, and acting as principal in financial products.

scenes.heading: Any technology
scenes.narration: Article 62 adds that the medium does not matter. Platforms, decentralized applications, protocols or DeFi that offer a licensed activity are still under the Central Bank's licensing and oversight.

scenes.heading: Register before you start
scenes.narration: Article 68 creates a public electronic register of licensed institutions. An institution may not begin any licensed activity until its name is entered on it.

cards.title: The licensing path for an institution

items.label: Apply to the Central Bank
items.detail: A person applies for a licence or to add an activity, under the board's regulations (Article 63(1)).

items.label: Meet the conditions
items.detail: Including fit and proper criteria, minimum capital, resources and control systems (Article 63(2)), plus any extra conditions.

items.label: Decision within 60 working days
items.detail: Counted from meeting all conditions; no answer by then counts as an implicit rejection (Article 64(1)).

items.label: Formal notice within 20 working days
items.detail: The applicant is officially told of the decision within 20 working days of its issue (Article 64(4)).

items.label: Entry on the register
items.detail: The licence decision is published in the Official Gazette and the name entered on the register (Article 68).

items.label: Start within the licence scope
items.detail: The institution operates only within the scope of its licence (Article 60(6)).

cards.title: Activity or approval?
cards.prompt: Sort each item: is it a licensed financial activity listed in Article 61, or a change that needs the Central Bank's prior approval?

items.text: Taking deposits from customers
Providing credit facilities
Providing open finance services
Instant money transfer services
Stored value and digital money services
Opening a new branch in Ajman (Art 121)
Amending the articles of association (Art 73)
Merging with another institution (Art 125)
Appointing a new board member (Art 130)
Ceasing a licensed activity (Art 126)

cards.question: Dunecrest applied to add a licensed activity. Seventy working days after it met every condition, the Central Bank has not replied. What does Article 64 say?
options: The silence counts as an implicit rejection of the application
The licence is deemed granted by silence after sixty working days
The bank may start the activity provisionally until a reply arrives
The application must be refiled with the Grievances and Appeals Committee
cards.explanation: Article 64(1) sets a decision period of up to sixty working days from meeting all conditions and treats expiry without a response as implicit rejection. There is no deemed approval or provisional start.

cards.title: Authorized Individuals and Designated Functions
cards.body:
Some roles influence a licensed institution so much that the **person** needs Central Bank approval too.

- **Article 107:** Designated Functions include those of board members, chief executives and other Authorized Individuals. Nobody may perform one without the Central Bank's **prior authorization**, and the institution must make sure no employee does.
- Authorized Individuals stay within the limits of their authorization; nobody may claim the status without it.
- **Article 108:** the institution applies for the individual, supplies the information requested and reports material changes.
- **Article 109:** a decision is due within 20 working days of meeting all conditions; silence counts as rejection, and a rejection can be grieved.
- **Articles 111-112:** the Central Bank may suspend, withdraw or revoke an authorization, for example for breaching fit and proper criteria or refusing to cooperate with examiners, and may bar an unfit person from licensed work.

cards.title: Appointing a new CFO the right way
cards.prompt: Put Dunecrest's steps for appointing a chief financial officer in the right order.
steps: Confirm with Compliance that the CFO role is a Designated Function
Dunecrest submits the authorization application to the Central Bank (Article 108)
Provide any further information the Central Bank asks for
Receive the Central Bank's decision, due within 20 working days of meeting all conditions
Only then let the CFO take up the role, within the authorization's limits
Notify the Central Bank later of any material change to the authorization conditions

lines.text: The authorization is still pending. Let's call him 'CFO designate' and have him sign off the quarter-end pack. It is only a title.
Signing off the financials is the function itself. The title doesn't matter if he is doing the job.
And Article 107 puts the duty on us as well as on him: we must make sure no employee performs a Designated Function without prior authorization.
What is the real risk? A warning letter?
Article 178 makes violating Article 107 a crime: at least a year's imprisonment and a fine of at least AED 500,000, plus a daily fine while it continues.

cards.title: The CFO designate
cards.situation: The new CFO has arrived, but the Central Bank has not yet decided on his authorization. The quarter-end pack must be signed in three days and the chief executive wants the new CFO to sign it as 'CFO designate'.

choices.text: Keep the authorized outgoing or interim signatory responsible for the pack, use the newcomer only in a support role and follow up the application with the Central Bank
choices.outcome: Best answer. The authorized person keeps the function, the newcomer learns the work without performing it, and Dunecrest meets its Article 107 duty to prevent unauthorized performance of a Designated Function.

choices.text: Let him sign as 'CFO designate' because the application is already filed
choices.outcome: Poor. Filing is not authorization. Article 107(3) requires prior authorization before anyone performs a Designated Function, and the title does not change what he is doing.

choices.text: Let him sign, but tell the Central Bank afterwards so it is on record
choices.outcome: Poor. Telling the Central Bank afterwards admits a breach. It does not cure it, and Article 178 attaches criminal penalties to violating Article 107.

choices.text: Delay the quarter-end pack until his authorization arrives
choices.outcome: Partly right. It avoids the unauthorized function but may breach reporting deadlines. The better route is to keep an authorized signatory in place.

items.label: Who is approved
items.right: An individual in a Designated Function

items.label: Decision period
items.left: Up to 60 working days after all conditions are met
items.right: Up to 20 working days after all conditions are met

items.label: Rejection challenge
items.left: Rejection on market capacity grounds is final, no grievance
items.right: Grievance to the Grievances and Appeals Committee

items.label: Criminal penalty
items.left: Unlicensed activity: up to AED 500m fine and/or prison (Art 170)
items.right: Breaching Art 107: at least 1 year prison and AED 500,000 (Art 178)

cards.front: Can a non-bank call itself a 'bank'?
cards.back: No. Only licensed banks may use 'Bank', 'Masraf' or similar terms in any language that could mislead the public (Article 67).

cards.front: What legal form must a bank take?
cards.back: A public joint-stock company, with exemptions for branches of foreign banks and specialised banks under the board's rules (Article 69).

cards.front: Minimum national shareholding in a bank incorporated in the UAE?
cards.back: At least 60%, under conditions the board sets (Article 71).

cards.front: Can a bank take its own shares as loan collateral?
cards.back: No. Article 119(3) forbids it.

cards.front: Can a deposit-taking bank run a trading business?
cards.back: No commercial or industrial business for its own account, except goods taken in settlement of debts and sold within the set period (Article 118).

cards.front: Who approves a new controlling shareholder?
cards.back: The Central Bank, in advance. The bank must not allow a controlling interest without that approval (Article 120).

cards.question: Under Article 130, which appointment at Dunecrest needs the Central Bank's prior approval?
options: Hiring a new branch customer service officer
Promoting an analyst within Regulatory Reporting
Renewing the employment contract of an Authorized Individual
Renewing a supplier contract for branch cleaning
cards.explanation: Article 130(2) requires prior Central Bank approval to nominate, appoint or renew board members and to appoint or renew the contracts of Authorized Individuals. Ordinary staff moves and supplier contracts are not covered.

cards.title: The influencer campaign (fictional)
cards.body:
Dunecrest's marketing team plans a social media campaign with a lifestyle influencer to promote a new instant transfer product, and also wants to 'white-label' the product through the fintech partner's app.

Layla's review asks four questions from the law:

1. **Is the activity licensed?** Money transfer is a licensed activity under Article 61; Dunecrest's licence must cover it.
2. **Is the promotion lawful?** Article 60(3) allows promotion only in line with the law and its rules, and treats any invitation to transact as promotion. The influencer's posts count.
3. **Is the partner doing a licensed activity itself?** If the partner arranges or markets the service, Article 61(1)(h) and Article 62 may bring it within licensing.
4. **Is anyone claiming a status they lack?** Article 60(7) bans presenting oneself as a licensed institution without being one.

The campaign goes ahead only after Legal confirms the partner's status and the posts are reviewed as financial promotions.

cards.title: Stage 2 take-aways
items: No licensed financial activity, and no promotion of one, without a Central Bank licence and within its scope (Articles 60-62).
Licence decisions are due within 60 working days of meeting all conditions; silence means rejection, and a name must be on the register before trading starts (Articles 64 and 68).
Board members, chief executives and other Authorized Individuals need prior authorization for their Designated Functions, decided within 20 working days (Articles 107-109).
Branches, amendments to the articles, controlling interests, mergers, cessation and board or Authorized Individual appointments all need prior Central Bank approval.
Breaching Article 107 is a crime carrying at least one year's imprisonment and an AED 500,000 minimum fine (Article 178).

cards.prompt: Think of a role in your bank that signs, approves or decides on behalf of the institution. Is it a Designated Function, and how would you check?

quiz.question: Which of these is listed in Article 61 as a licensed financial activity?
options: Running a staff canteen at head office
Renting safe office space to fintech firms
Providing open finance services
Providing payroll software to employers
quiz.explanation: Article 61(1)(d) lists open finance services. Software, office rental and canteens are not financial activities under the law.

quiz.question: An exchange house advertises instant transfers on billboards before its licence is granted. Which provisions are engaged?
options: Only the rules on currency mutilation (Article 59)
Only the reserve requirement rules (Article 32)
The bans on unlicensed activity and on unlawful promotion (Article 60)
Only the rules on related-party lending, because the billboard names a related company (Article 116)
quiz.explanation: Article 60 bans carrying on licensed activities without a licence and limits promotion of licensed activities to what the law allows; advertising is promotion. The other articles deal with currency, reserves and related-party statements.

quiz.question: Within what period must the Central Bank decide on a licence application, counted from when all conditions are met?
options: Up to twenty working days
Up to six calendar months
Up to sixty working days
Up to ten working days
quiz.explanation: Article 64(1) sets up to sixty working days from meeting all licensing conditions. Twenty working days is the period for notifying decisions and for deciding on individual authorizations.

quiz.question: Dunecrest's application to add an activity is rejected because the Central Bank judges the market has enough capacity. Can Dunecrest file a grievance?
options: No. A rejection on sector capacity and market needs is final and cannot be grieved
No, unless the Minister of Finance agrees to review it
Yes, within twenty working days of the notice, in the same way as any other Central Bank decision
Yes, but only through the Higher Federal Court directly
quiz.explanation: Article 64(3) makes rejections based on the sector's capacity and local market needs final and not subject to appeal before the Grievances and Appeals Committee. Most other decisions can be grieved within twenty working days.

quiz.question: Which of these roles does Article 107(2) expressly name as Designated Functions needing authorization?
options: Members of the board of directors and chief executive officers
Shareholders owning more than five percent
External auditors of the institution
All customer-facing branch staff
quiz.explanation: Article 107(2) names board members, chief executive officers and other Authorized Individuals. Branch staff and shareholders are not named, and auditors are regulated under Article 140.

quiz.question: A newly hired chief risk officer starts approving limits the week before her authorization is decided. Who has breached Article 107?
options: Nobody, because the authorization application had already been submitted to the Central Bank
Only Dunecrest, because employees cannot breach the law
Both she and Dunecrest, which must stop unauthorized performance
Only she, because the duty is personal to the individual
quiz.explanation: Article 107(3) bars any individual from performing a Designated Function without prior authorization, and Article 107(4) requires the institution to ensure no officer or employee does. A pending application is not authorization.

quiz.question: What happens to an Authorized Individual's authorization when he leaves Dunecrest for another job?
options: It is suspended until the Grievances Committee rules
It stays valid for one year in case he returns
It transfers automatically to his new employer
It is revoked, because his relationship with the institution has ended
quiz.explanation: Article 111(2) says the authorization is revoked in all cases when the institution applies to cancel it or the person's relationship with the institution ends. It does not transfer or survive.

quiz.question: Dunecrest wants to open a representative office abroad and close a branch in Sharjah. What does Article 121 require?
options: The Central Bank's prior approval
No approval if the branch is outside the State
A notification to the Central Bank within thirty days after the change
Approval of the general assembly only
quiz.explanation: Article 121 bars establishing any branch or subsidiary inside or outside the State, or relocating or closing an existing branch, without prior Central Bank approval. After-the-fact notice and shareholder approval alone are not enough.

quiz.question: A customer's company wants a loan secured on Dunecrest's own shares, which it owns. What does the law say?
options: It may, up to the ratio set by the Central Bank's board
Dunecrest may not take its own shares as collateral for customer credit
It may, if the shares are listed on a UAE market
It may, if the loan is approved by the board of Dunecrest
quiz.explanation: Article 119(3) prohibits a licensed institution from taking its own shares as collateral when providing credit to customers. No ratio or approval exception appears.

quiz.question: A trading company in Dubai names itself 'Golden Sands Masraf Trading'. It is not a licensed bank. What is the issue?
options: None, because 'Masraf' is an Arabic word in a trading name rather than a regulated legal term
None, unless the company actually takes deposits
Only a tax issue under the trade licence rules
Article 67 bars non-banks from misleading use of 'Bank' or 'Masraf'
quiz.explanation: Article 67 prohibits entities other than licensed banks from using 'Bank', 'Masraf' or derived or similar expressions in any language in a way that could mislead. Article 177 attaches criminal penalties. Taking deposits is not required for the breach.

sessions.title: Customer Protection: Confidentiality, Complaints, Fair Credit and Fraud
sessions.summary: Customer data confidentiality and its exceptions, complaint decisions and the Central Bank's independent unit, the ban on compound interest, guarantees for lending to individuals, and the new fraud prevention duties.
objectives: Apply the confidentiality duty and its listed exceptions in Article 147
Explain complaint decisions, written reasons and the independent unit's dispute thresholds (Article 148)
Recognise the ban on compound interest and the guarantee rule for credit to individuals
Apply the fraud prevention, customer notice and cooperation duties in Article 149

cards.title: The phishing call
cards.setting: Dunecrest Bank, Dubai Marina branch. Monday, 10:00 am.

lines.text: A customer, Mrs Fatima Rahimi, arrives upset. A caller claiming to be from the bank talked her into sharing a one-time code, and AED 18,000 left her account overnight.
Classic social engineering. Article 149 names it, along with unauthorized transactions and identity theft, as risks our controls must guard against.
Meanwhile her brother phoned the call centre asking for her balance 'to help'. The agent nearly told him.
That would have been a second breach. Customer data is confidential under Article 147 unless she consents or the law allows it.
And if she complains and we say no, the law requires written reasons. Let's make sure today goes by the book.
Stage three: the customer side of the law. Confidentiality, complaints, fair credit and fraud.

cards.title: The customer chapter of the law

scenes.heading: Confidential by default
scenes.narration: Article 147 makes all data about customers, their accounts and transactions confidential. It may not be viewed or disclosed to anyone without the customer's consent, or that of their lawyer or authorized agent, except where the law allows.

scenes.heading: Complaints with reasons
scenes.narration: Article 148 says banks must decide on every complaint and, if they reject it in whole or part, give the reasons in writing. Customers can then take the dispute to the independent unit the Central Bank sets up.

scenes.heading: No interest on interest
scenes.narration: Article 148(11) forbids licensed institutions from charging interest on accrued interest, that is compound interest, on facilities to customers, following the Central Bank's rules.

scenes.heading: Robust fraud defences
scenes.narration: Article 149 requires robust fraud prevention and detection, prompt notice to affected customers, immediate corrective action and full cooperation with Central Bank fraud investigations.

scenes.heading: Clear information
scenes.narration: Article 149(7) also requires clear, transparent and easily accessible information on fees, terms and risks, so customers can make informed decisions.

items.label: Prevent and detect
items.detail: Robust mechanisms against unauthorized transactions, social engineering and identity theft (149(1)).

items.label: Notify customers promptly
items.detail: Tell affected customers of security breaches or fraud incidents without delay (149(3)).

items.label: Correct immediately
items.detail: Take immediate corrective action to limit the damage (149(3)).

items.label: Share data with the regulator
items.detail: Provide transaction records, fraud patterns and mitigation measures when the Central Bank asks (149(4)).

items.label: Cooperate and implement
items.detail: Cooperate with Central Bank fraud investigations and apply its preventive measures within its deadlines (149(5)).

cards.title: Can Dunecrest disclose it?
cards.prompt: Under Article 147, may Dunecrest disclose the customer information in each case?

items.text: The customer's account statement to a judicial authority acting under its legal powers
Account records the bank's external auditors need for their audit
A certificate of the reasons for not paying a cheque, issued to the cheque's beneficiary
Transaction data the bank needs to prove its claim in a legal dispute with that customer
Customer files transferred to the buyer in a Central Bank-approved acquisition
The balance, given to the customer's brother who says he is helping her
A list of high-balance customers, shared with an insurance partner for marketing
A former customer's address, given to a debt buyer without consent or legal basis

cards.question: A customer closed his account three years ago. A former colleague asks a Dunecrest employee about his old transactions. What does Article 147 say?
options: The duty ends when the account closes, so disclosure is allowed
The confidentiality duty continues after the relationship ends, so the employee must not disclose
Disclosure is allowed after two years if the data is anonymised
Only the branch manager may decide whether to disclose
cards.explanation: Article 147(2) says the prohibition stays valid even after the business relationship ends for any reason, and 147(3) binds employees personally. No time limit or managerial discretion appears.

cards.title: Complaints and the independent unit (Article 148)
cards.body:
**Inside the bank**
- Banks must handle every complaint or claim under the contract terms and the law, and **issue a decision** on it.
- If a complaint is rejected in whole or in part, the bank must give its **reasons in writing** (148(3)).

**Outside the bank**
- The Central Bank establishes an **independent unit with legal personality** to receive and decide customer complaints against banks and insurers, with binding resolutions (148(2)).
- A customer in dispute with a bank may file a complaint with that unit (148(4)).
- Its dispute committees are each headed by a judge, with another judge and one or more experts (148(5)).
- For disputes **up to AED 100,000**, committee resolutions are final and enforceable against the bank (148(6)).
- For disputes **above AED 100,000**, either side may challenge before the Court of Appeal **within 30 days** (148(7)).

Check the Central Bank's current rules for the unit's name, procedures and fees.

cards.title: Customer protections and where they sit
cards.prompt: Match each protection to its provision in Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025.

pairs.right: Customer data stays confidential, even after the relationship ends
Rejected complaints must be answered with written reasons
No interest charged on accrued interest for customer facilities
Limited sharing with another licensed institution to verify suspected fraud
Guarantees for credit to individuals must match income and facility size
Everyone has a right to access services suited to their needs

lines.text: Tomás, look at this collections spreadsheet. Overdue interest is added to the balance each month and then charged interest again.
That is interest on accrued interest. Article 148(11) bans it on facilities to customers.
The collections head says it has always been done this way and the contracts allow it.
A contract term cannot override the law. And remember Article 168: the Central Bank can order a bank to return funds it gained through a violation.

cards.title: Interest on interest
cards.situation: Dunecrest's collections system capitalises unpaid interest on overdue personal loans every month, so later interest is charged on it. The loan contracts mention this method. The collections head wants to keep it until the Central Bank issues detailed rules.

choices.text: Stop the compounding now, escalate to Compliance and the board, quantify affected customers and prepare to refund, applying any Central Bank rules on the method
choices.outcome: Best answer. Article 148(11) prohibits compound interest on customer facilities, and Article 168(1)(k) lets the Central Bank require funds obtained through a violation to be returned. Acting early limits harm and shows good faith.

choices.text: Keep compounding until detailed Central Bank rules arrive, because contracts allow it
choices.outcome: Poor. The ban is in the law itself. The Central Bank's rules govern how to apply it, not whether it applies, and a contract term cannot override the law.

choices.text: Stop compounding on new loans only and leave existing loans unchanged
choices.outcome: Partly right. It stops new harm but leaves existing customers paying interest on interest. The law applies to facilities extended to customers, so existing balances need review too.

choices.text: Rename the charge as a 'late service fee' calculated the same way
choices.outcome: Poor. Renaming does not change the substance, and it would also fail the duty in Article 149(7) to give clear and transparent information on fees.

cards.title: Where a customer dispute ends up
cards.caption: Article 148(6)-(7) of Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025.

items.label: Committee resolution
items.left: Final and enforceable against the bank

items.label: Challenge
items.right: Either party may go to the Court of Appeal

items.label: Time limit
items.right: 30 days from issue or knowledge of it

cards.front: Which fraud types does 149(1) name?
cards.back: Unauthorized transactions, social engineering, identity theft and other fraudulent activities.

cards.front: What may the Central Bank set under 149(2)?
cards.back: Minimum security standards for digital and traditional banking, such as authentication, transaction monitoring and reporting of suspected fraud.

cards.front: What must a bank do after a breach or fraud?
cards.back: Promptly notify the affected customers and take immediate corrective action to limit the damage (149(3)).

cards.front: What data may the Central Bank demand?
cards.back: Transaction records, fraud patterns, mitigation measures and other information to monitor risk and issue sector-wide directives (149(4)).

cards.front: Can banks share data about a suspected fraudster?
cards.back: Yes, with another licensed institution authorized to receive it, only as far as needed for verification, when there are reasonable concerns (149(6)).

cards.question: Dunecrest has reasonable concerns that a customer is moving fraudulent payments to another UAE bank. What does Article 149(6) allow?
options: Publishing the customer's name on social media to warn others
Sharing the customer's full file with any business that asks
Nothing, because Article 147 forbids every disclosure
Sharing documents or information about that customer with the other licensed institution, only as far as needed to verify
cards.explanation: Article 149(6), without prejudice to Article 147, lets a licensed institution disclose a customer's documents or information to another licensed institution authorized to receive them, limited to what verification needs, when reasonable concerns of suspicious or fraudulent transactions arise.

cards.title: Handling Mrs Rahimi's case (fictional)
cards.body:
Tomás runs the case against Article 149 and the confidentiality rules:

- **Contain:** block the compromised channel, reset credentials and try to recall the transfer at once (immediate corrective action, 149(3)).
- **Tell the customer:** explain promptly and in writing what happened and what the bank is doing (149(3)).
- **Check the controls:** why did authentication and transaction monitoring not stop a new payee and an unusual overnight transfer? Log the gap.
- **Verify with the other bank:** share only what is needed to verify the receiving account with that licensed bank (149(6)).
- **Keep the brother out:** no disclosure without Mrs Rahimi's consent (147).
- **Decide the complaint:** if the bank declines to refund in full, give written reasons and tell her she can take the dispute to the Central Bank's independent unit (148).
- **Feed the regulator:** record the incident so fraud data and patterns can be reported when the Central Bank asks (149(4)).

cards.title: Plain words beat small print
cards.body: Article 149(7) asks for information on fees, terms and risks that is **clear, transparent and easy to find**. Before launching or changing a product, test the key facts sheet on a colleague outside the team: can they say what it costs, what can go wrong and how to complain in under a minute? If not, rewrite it. Clear disclosure also prevents many complaints that would otherwise reach the Central Bank's independent unit.

cards.title: Stage 3 take-aways
items: Customer data is confidential; disclose only with consent or under a listed legal exception, and the duty survives account closure (Article 147).
Intentionally breaching customer confidentiality is a crime: imprisonment and/or a fine of AED 100,000 to 500,000 (Article 171).
Decide every complaint and give written reasons for rejections; the Central Bank's unit decides disputes, finally up to AED 100,000 (Article 148).
Compound interest on customer facilities is banned (Article 148(11)), and guarantees for lending to individuals must match income and facility size (Article 150).
Run robust fraud prevention, notify customers promptly, correct immediately, share data with the Central Bank and cooperate with its investigations (Article 149).

cards.prompt: Recall the last time a customer asked about someone else's account or a charge they did not understand. What did you do, and what would the 2025 law expect?

quiz.question: A woman calls asking for her husband's card balance, saying they share finances. He has given no consent. What should the agent do?
options: Give the balance, because spouses who share finances count as authorized agents under the law
Give an approximate balance rather than the exact figure
Give the balance only if she knows his date of birth
Decline, because she has no consent or legal basis to receive it
quiz.explanation: Article 147(1) allows disclosure only with the consent of the customer, their lawyer or authorized agent, or in legally authorized cases. A spouse is not automatically an agent, and partial or approximate disclosure is still disclosure.

quiz.question: Which of these is an exception to customer confidentiality listed in Article 147(6)?
options: The bank sharing customer lists with partners for joint marketing
The bank disclosing balances to relatives in emergencies
Disclosing data the bank needs to establish its rights in a dispute with that customer
The bank publishing the names of its largest depositors in its annual report to show its strength
quiz.explanation: Article 147(6)(e) preserves the bank's right to disclose transaction data to establish its rights in a legal dispute with the customer. Marketing, relatives and annual report publication are not exceptions.

quiz.question: Dunecrest rejects a customer's complaint about a disputed card fee. What must it do under Article 148(3)?
options: Refer the complaint automatically to the Central Bank
State the reasons for the rejection in writing
Refund half the fee as a goodwill gesture
Ask the customer to sign a waiver before closing the file
quiz.explanation: Article 148(3) requires banks to decide on every complaint and, where they reject it in whole or part, to give written reasons. Automatic referral, partial refunds and waivers are not required.

quiz.question: A customer wins AED 80,000 against Dunecrest before the Central Bank's dispute committee. Dunecrest wants to appeal. What does the law say?
options: The bank may appeal to the Higher Federal Court within 20 working days
The bank may refuse to pay until the Grievances Committee reviews it
The bank may appeal to the Court of Appeal within 30 days
The resolution is final and enforceable, and the bank cannot challenge it
quiz.explanation: Article 148(6) makes committee resolutions final and enforceable against banks for disputes up to AED 100,000. The 30-day Court of Appeal route in 148(7) applies only above that value.

quiz.question: Which practice does Article 148(11) prohibit?
options: Charging any interest at all on customer loans
Charging different rates to retail and corporate customers
Charging fees for issuing account certificates
Charging interest on accrued interest on facilities extended to customers
quiz.explanation: Article 148(11) bans compound interest, meaning interest on accrued interest, on customer facilities. It does not ban interest, fees or differentiated pricing.

quiz.question: Fraud monitoring flags an account takeover on a customer's mobile banking. Which pair of actions does Article 149(3) require?
options: Notify the Central Bank first and contact the affected customer only after the Central Bank replies
Close the file and wait for the customer to call
Promptly notify the customer and take immediate corrective action
Freeze all the customer's accounts permanently
quiz.explanation: Article 149(3) requires prompt notice to affected customers and immediate corrective action. Waiting for the customer or for the Central Bank delays both duties, and permanent freezing is not what the law asks.

quiz.question: Which three fraud risks does Article 149(1) expressly name?
options: Cheque kiting, forgery and counterfeit coins
Unauthorized transactions, social engineering and identity theft
Tax evasion, bribery and cartel conduct
Insider trading, market abuse and short selling
quiz.explanation: Article 149(1) names unauthorized transactions, social engineering and identity theft, plus other fraudulent activities. The other lists are real risks but not those named in the article.

quiz.question: A loan officer wants to lend to a self-employed sole proprietor without checking that the guarantee and size of the facility fit his income. What risk does Article 150 create for Dunecrest?
options: None, because Article 150 applies only to corporate borrowers and not to sole proprietorships
If guarantees were not obtained and kept, its later claim may be inadmissible
Only a higher capital charge on the loan
Only a duty to report the loan to the credit bureau
quiz.explanation: Article 150 requires adequate guarantees for facilities to natural persons and sole proprietorships, commensurate with income and facility size, and makes the bank's claims inadmissible if it failed to obtain or maintain them. The Central Bank may also impose sanctions.

quiz.question: Under Article 152, what right does every person have?
options: To access all or part of the banking and financial services suited to their needs
To receive a credit card from at least one bank
To borrow at the Central Bank's base rate
To open an account without any identity checks
quiz.explanation: Article 152(1) tasks the Central Bank's board with ensuring every person can access banking and financial services suited to their needs. It does not create a right to credit, waive identity checks or set borrowing rates.

quiz.question: A Dunecrest employee deliberately sends a celebrity customer's statements to a journalist. Which consequence does the law provide?
options: Only an internal warning under the bank's code of conduct, because no money was taken
Imprisonment and/or a fine of AED 100,000 to 500,000
Only a civil claim by the customer for damages
A fine on the journalist but none on the employee
quiz.explanation: Article 171(2) punishes whoever intentionally discloses data protected by Article 147 with imprisonment and a fine of AED 100,000 to 500,000, or either. Internal discipline and civil claims may follow, but the criminal penalty is in the law.

sessions.title: Regulatory Reporting by Qualified Staff (Article 122)
sessions.summary: The core of the quest: the duty to appoint qualified reporting staff and give them the data they need, the ban on withholding information, immediate reporting of significant matters, year-end packages, audit and publication duties.
objectives: Explain the duties in Article 122 and the personal exposure of reporting staff
Distinguish immediate reporting under Article 123 from periodic statements and public disclosures
Apply the deadlines for related-party statements, audited accounts and the audit report
Respond correctly to pressure to delay, withhold or alter reported information

cards.title: Quarter-end at the reporting desk
cards.setting: Regulatory Reporting, Dunecrest head office. Last working day of the quarter, 6:00 pm.

lines.text: Treasury still hasn't sent the related-party exposure data. Without it I can't build the quarterly statement.
Then we escalate tonight. Article 122 says the bank must make sure the people preparing Central Bank reports get the information they need.
An email arrives from a business head: 'Please hold back the large exposure figure until we restructure the deal next month. No need to trouble the Central Bank.'
Can he even ask that?
No. The law forbids a bank from instructing or agreeing with any manager or employee to withhold what the Central Bank requires.
This is the heart of the quest. Article 122 is why reporting staff must be qualified, supported and independent enough to say no.

scenes.heading: Provide what is required
scenes.narration: Licensed institutions must give the Central Bank the reports, information, statements and documents it decides it needs to meet its objectives and do its job.

scenes.heading: Qualified people
scenes.narration: They must appoint qualified employees and give them the task of preparing the reports the Central Bank requires.

scenes.heading: Access to information
scenes.narration: They must take appropriate measures so those employees actually get the information needed to prepare the reports.

scenes.heading: No gagging
scenes.narration: A bank may not instruct, or agree with, any manager, officer, employee, agent or auditor to decline to provide the Central Bank with what it requires.

scenes.heading: Personal exposure
scenes.narration: The Central Bank sets the nature, forms and frequency of reporting, and it may take measures against the institution or against the employees assigned to prepare the reports.

items.label: Financial year closes 31 December
items.detail: A licensed institution's financial year runs January to December (Article 138).

items.label: Audited statements to the Central Bank
items.detail: Within three months of year end, or another set period: audited balance sheet, P&L, auditors' and board reports (Article 124(1)).

items.label: Audit report before the general assembly
items.detail: Send the auditors' report, balance sheet and P&L at least 20 working days before the general assembly (Article 140(1)).

items.label: Central Bank remarks and dividends
items.detail: The assembly waits for the Central Bank's remarks; within 10 working days it may block proposed profit distribution (Article 140(2)).

items.label: General assembly reads the reports
items.detail: Accounts go to the assembly only after Central Bank approval (Article 124(3)).

items.label: Publish within 20 working days
items.detail: After approval, publish the reports on the website within 20 working days of the assembly and post them in branches (Articles 140(3), 141).

cards.question: Under Article 122(1)(b), what must Dunecrest do about the people who prepare its Central Bank reports?
options: Outsource all reporting to the external auditor
Have the chief executive personally prepare every report
Appoint qualified employees and assign them the task of preparing the required reports
Rotate reporting among all finance staff each quarter
cards.explanation: Article 122(1)(b) requires the appointment of qualified employees assigned to prepare the Central Bank's required reports, and 122(1)(c) requires measures so they get the information they need. Outsourcing, rotation or CEO preparation are not what the article sets.

cards.title: What 'qualified' means in practice
cards.body:
Article 122 does not define *qualified*. The Central Bank may issue regulations and instructions on how reports are provided (122(6)), and it sets the **nature, forms and frequency** of submissions (122(4)). Until you have checked those rules, build a defensible standard of your own:

- **Knowledge:** the 2025 law's reporting articles (116, 122-124, 140-141), the Central Bank's current reporting instructions and the bank's data sources.
- **Skills:** reconciling returns to the general ledger, applying definitions consistently, documenting judgements.
- **Independence:** reporting staff can escalate pressure without fear; Article 122(2) bans gagging instructions.
- **Evidence:** role profiles, training records, supervision and review sign-offs.

The stakes are personal: Article 122(6) lets the Central Bank act against the assigned employees, and Article 179 punishes misleading, incomplete or concealed information.

cards.title: Preparing a Central Bank return
cards.prompt: Put the steps a qualified reporting analyst should follow in a sensible order.
steps: Check the current Central Bank instruction for the return's form, definitions and frequency
Request source data from the business owners, escalating if it is not provided
Reconcile the figures to the general ledger and to prior periods
Document judgements and any data limitations
Obtain independent review and sign-off by the accountable manager
Submit on time and keep the working papers for examiners

items.label: Related-party statement
items.detail: Quarterly statement of credit to related parties, due within 10 working days of quarter end or a request (Article 116(2)).

items.label: Audited year-end package
items.detail: Audited balance sheet, P&L, auditors' and board reports within three months of year end (Article 124(1)).

items.label: Before the general assembly
items.detail: Auditors' report, balance sheet and P&L to the Central Bank at least 20 working days ahead (Article 140(1)).

items.label: Minimum criminal fine
items.detail: For misleading, incomplete or concealed information given to the Central Bank, with possible imprisonment (Article 179).

lines.text: The business head says the exposure will be restructured next month anyway, so reporting it now just causes noise.
The return must show the position as it is at the reporting date. A plan to fix it later is something we can explain, not something we can hide.
And if the breach is significant, Article 123 may require us to report it to the Central Bank immediately, not just in the return.
What if he complains about me to HR?

For compliance officers, legal representatives and auditors who report in good faith, Article 123 says the bank cannot dismiss or discipline them without the Central Bank's approval. And gagging staff is itself banned by Article 122(2).

cards.title: The email from the business head
cards.situation: It is quarter-end. A senior business head asks Arjun in writing to leave a large exposure out of the return because a restructuring next month will cure it. The figure is correct and the return is due tomorrow.

choices.text: Report the true figure, add context on the planned restructuring, escalate the email to Noura and Compliance, and assess whether Article 123 requires an immediate report
choices.outcome: Best answer. Article 122 requires complete reporting and bans instructions to withhold, Article 179 punishes incomplete or concealed information, and Article 123 may require immediate notice of a significant matter or violation.

choices.text: Leave the figure out this quarter and include it next quarter when it is smaller
choices.outcome: Poor. This conceals a fact from the Central Bank, which Article 179 makes a crime carrying a fine of at least AED 500,000 and possible imprisonment.

choices.text: Report the figure but say nothing about the email to avoid conflict
choices.outcome: Partly right. The return is accurate, but the instruction to withhold is itself a breach of Article 122(2) and a governance issue the bank must address.

choices.text: Ask the Central Bank for a filing extension until the restructuring is done
choices.outcome: Poor. An extension to wait for a cure would delay accurate reporting for no valid reason, and would hide the position at the reporting date.

cards.title: Which reporting channel?
cards.prompt: Sort each item by the reporting duty it falls under.

items.text: A Matter of Significance that may affect the bank's structure or position
A violation of the 2025 law or of Central Bank regulations
A serious financial or administrative situation endangering customers' rights
Quarterly statement of credit facilities to board members and related companies
Audited balance sheet and profit and loss account after year end
Semi-annual interim P&L if the Central Bank asks for it
Names of board members, senior executives and Authorized Individuals
Names of all wholly or partly owned subsidiaries

cards.title: Articles of the reporting toolkit
cards.prompt: Match each article to the reporting duty it sets.

pairs.right: Quarterly statement of credit to directors and other related parties
Qualified staff prepare required reports and get the information they need
Immediate reporting of significant matters and violations, with good-faith protection
Financial position data and the audited year-end package
Approved auditors and the audit report before the general assembly
Publishing accounts and key names on the website and in every branch

cards.question: Who carries the duty in Article 123 to report a Matter of Significance or a violation to the Central Bank immediately?
options: Only the chief executive, after board approval
The institution, its legal representatives, its compliance officers and its auditors
Only the external auditor, once a year
Only customers who were harmed by the violation
cards.explanation: Article 123(1) places the immediate reporting duty on the licensed institution together with its legal representatives, compliance officers and auditors, and 123(2) protects them when they report in good faith.

cards.title: How Dunecrest defines 'qualified' (fictional)
cards.body:
Because Article 122 does not define the term, Noura writes a one-page standard that the board approves:

- **Role profile** for each reporting analyst, reviewer and the head of reporting.
- **Entry requirement:** a finance, accounting or risk qualification or equivalent experience, plus induction on the 2025 law and the Central Bank's reporting instructions.
- **Ongoing learning:** a yearly plan covering new instructions, definitions and data changes, with hours logged.
- **Four-eyes review** on every return, with documented sign-off.
- **Access rights:** a standing instruction from the chief executive that business units must give reporting staff the data they ask for, on time (122(1)(c)).
- **Speak-up route:** pressure to withhold goes straight to Compliance.

If an examiner asks *how do you know your reporting staff are qualified?*, Dunecrest can show the standard, the records and the reviews.

cards.title: Make the data come to you
cards.body: Most late or wrong returns start with missing data, not bad arithmetic. Agree a **data calendar** with each business owner, name a backup contact, and record every late or incomplete delivery. Article 122(1)(c) puts the duty on the bank to make sure reporting staff get the information they need, so a pattern of late data is a governance issue to escalate, not something to absorb quietly.

cards.title: Stage 4 take-aways
items: Article 122 requires qualified employees assigned to prepare Central Bank reports, with measures that get them the information they need.
No one may be instructed or agreed with to withhold information from the Central Bank (122(2)), and the Central Bank may act against the bank or the assigned employees (122(6)).
Report Matters of Significance and violations immediately (Article 123); compliance officers and auditors who report in good faith are protected.
Know the deadlines: related-party statement in 10 working days, audited package within three months, audit report 20 working days before the assembly.
Misleading, incomplete or concealed information is a crime with a fine of at least AED 500,000 and possible imprisonment (Article 179).

cards.prompt: If an examiner asked you tomorrow how you know a figure you report is complete and correct, what evidence could you show?

quiz.question: Under Article 122(1)(c), what must Dunecrest do for the employees preparing Central Bank reports?
options: Take appropriate measures so they obtain the information needed to prepare the reports
Give them a seat on the board's risk committee
Exempt them from the bank's internal audit reviews
Pay them a fixed bonus for each return filed on time
quiz.explanation: Article 122(1)(c) requires appropriate measures to ensure the assigned employees get the information required. Bonuses, audit exemptions and board seats are not part of the duty.

quiz.question: A department head tells his team not to send data to the Central Bank's reporting team until 'legal has looked at it', with no end date. Which provision is engaged?
options: Article 67, which restricts use of the word 'bank'
Article 147, which protects customer confidentiality and so justifies a pause while legal reviews the data
Article 132, which bars retroactive regulations
Article 122(2), which bans telling staff to withhold required information
quiz.explanation: Article 122(2) prohibits instructions or agreements with managers, officers, employees, agents or auditors to decline to provide the Central Bank with required information. Confidentiality does not limit disclosure to the Central Bank, whose powers are preserved by 147(6)(a).

quiz.question: Who decides the form and frequency of the information banks submit to the Central Bank?
options: The Central Bank, through its instructions
The external auditor, in its engagement letter
Each bank's board, in its reporting policy
The Ministry of Finance, in the federal budget
quiz.explanation: Article 122(4) gives the Central Bank power to determine the nature, forms and frequency of submissions, and banks must follow its instructions.

quiz.question: Does Article 122 apply to the UAE branch of a foreign bank?
options: Only after its first full year of operation
No, branches of foreign banks report only to their home regulator through head office
Yes, Article 122(5) extends it to foreign branches in the State
Only if the branch takes retail deposits
quiz.explanation: Article 122(5) expressly extends the reporting duties to branches of foreign licensed financial institutions operating in the UAE.

quiz.question: Within what period must Dunecrest send the Central Bank its quarterly related-party credit statement?
options: At the next general assembly meeting
Within three months of the end of the financial year
Within thirty calendar days of the end of each quarter, together with the quarterly accounts
Within ten working days of each quarter end or of a request
quiz.explanation: Article 116(2) requires a copy of the related-party statement within ten working days of each quarter end or of a Central Bank request. Three months is the audited year-end deadline in Article 124.

quiz.question: Dunecrest's board wants to present the year-end accounts to the general assembly next week, but the Central Bank has not yet approved them. What does Article 124(3) say?
options: The bank may present them and seek approval afterwards
The bank may not present them to the general assembly before the Central Bank's approval
The bank may present them if the board votes unanimously
The bank may present them if the auditor has signed
quiz.explanation: Article 124(3) bars presenting the financial position data and reports to the general assembly before Central Bank approval, and Article 140(2) says the assembly is not convened before the Central Bank's remarks on the audit report.

quiz.question: Dunecrest's compliance officer reports a violation to the Central Bank in good faith. The chief executive wants to dismiss her. What does Article 123(2) require?
options: The bank may dismiss her if the board agrees by majority and records its reasons in the minutes
The bank must first pay her one year's salary
Obtain the Central Bank's approval before dismissing or disciplining her
The bank may dismiss her after a 30-day notice period
quiz.explanation: Article 123(2) protects those in 123(1) who report in good faith and bars the institution from dismissing them or taking disciplinary action without Central Bank approval.

quiz.question: Arjun discovers that last quarter's return understated an exposure because of a data mapping error. What should happen?
options: Delete the working papers so the error cannot be traced
Correct and resubmit promptly with an explanation, fix the mapping and assess Article 123
Leave it, because the next return will show the right number
Correct it quietly in the next return without explanation, since the error was unintentional and small
quiz.explanation: Accurate reporting under Article 122 and the ban on misleading or incomplete information in Article 179 point to prompt correction with an explanation. Destroying documents could itself be an offence under Article 179(3).

quiz.question: Which of these must Dunecrest publish on its website and post in each of its branches under Article 141?
options: Its audited accounts, the auditors' report and the names of board members and Authorized Individuals
Its regulatory returns submitted during the year
Its full list of related-party loans with amounts, borrowers and interest rates, posted on the website for public scrutiny
Its internal audit reports and compliance findings
quiz.explanation: Article 141(1) requires publication of the audited balance sheet, P&L and auditors' report, names of board members, senior executives and Authorized Individuals, and subsidiaries. Internal reports and returns are not public disclosures.

quiz.question: Under Article 124(4), what must Authorized Individuals do if the bank faces a serious financial or administrative situation that threatens customers' rights?
options: Wait for the next quarterly return to report it
Promptly notify the Central Bank
Ask the auditor to decide whether it is serious
Inform shareholders before anyone else
quiz.explanation: Article 124(4) requires Authorized Individuals to notify the Central Bank promptly when the institution is exposed to serious financial or administrative situations compromising customers' rights.

sessions.title: Examinations, Sanctions, Appeals and Assessment Readiness
sessions.summary: How Central Bank examinations work, the Article 168 sanctions and criminal penalties, grievances and appeals, personal liability of managers, early intervention and resolution, and the evidence file that proves readiness.
objectives: Describe the Central Bank's examination powers and the institution's duties during an examination
Explain the range and procedure of administrative sanctions and the main criminal penalties
Apply the grievance and appeal routes and deadlines in Article 167
Assemble a readiness file covering governance, reporting, customers and transition
