cards.title: The examiners arrive
cards.setting: Dunecrest head office, Abu Dhabi. Monday, 8:00 am.

lines.text: A Central Bank examination team arrives with a request list: governance files, authorizations, complaints, fraud incidents and three years of returns.
Can they just turn up like this?
Yes. Article 133 lets the Central Bank send its staff, or a third party acting for it, at any time to check our soundness and compliance.
And we must give them everything on the subject of the examination, on time. They can also summon people to provide information.
Someone in Operations is asking whether they should tidy up the fraud log first.
Nobody alters anything. The final stage: examinations, sanctions, appeals, and the file that proves we are ready.

cards.title: When the Central Bank finds a problem

scenes.heading: Examination
scenes.narration: Under Article 133 the Central Bank can examine a licensed institution and its subsidiaries at any time, demand records on a timely basis and summon any related person to provide information.

scenes.heading: Supervisory measures
scenes.narration: If it finds a violation it can restrict activities, order immediate rectification, appoint an expert or a Central Bank employee to advise or oversee operations, and impose sanctions under Article 168.

scenes.heading: Sanctions menu
scenes.narration: Article 168 ranges from a caution to fines of up to one billion dirhams on an institution, fines on Authorized Individuals, removal of individuals, and revocation of the licence.

scenes.heading: Grievance and appeal
scenes.narration: Most Central Bank decisions can be challenged before the Grievances and Appeals Committee within 20 working days, and its decision before the Higher Federal Court within another 20 working days.

scenes.heading: Personal liability
scenes.narration: Under Article 181, where a company commits an offence, the manager in charge can face the same penalties if he knew of it or it resulted from his negligence.

cards.title: The sanctions ladder (Article 168)
cards.caption: Most sanctions are decided by the Governor; licence revocation is decided by the Central Bank's board.

items.label: Licence revoked
items.detail: Licence revoked and name struck off the register, decided by the Central Bank's board (168(1)(o), 168(2)).

items.label: Individuals removed or barred
items.detail: Removal of Authorized Individuals, or a ban on working at any licensed institution (168(1)(e), (r)).

items.label: Heavy fines
items.detail: Up to AED 1bn on an institution, up to 10 times the amount involved, AED 100,000-5m on an individual (168(1)(l), (m), (q)).

items.label: Restrictions and deposits
items.detail: Limits on activities, reduced access to Central Bank facilities, non-interest deposits (168(1)(c), (d), (i)).

items.label: Remedial orders and refunds
items.detail: Orders to rectify and to return funds to customers (168(1)(b), (k)).

items.label: Caution
items.detail: A caution issued to the violator by any means (168(1)(a)).

cards.question: Who decides to revoke a bank's licence as a sanction under Article 168?
options: The Governor alone, like every other sanction
The Grievances and Appeals Committee
The Minister of Finance on the Governor's proposal
The Central Bank's board of directors
cards.explanation: Article 168(2) says sanctions are imposed by the Governor except licence revocation and striking off under 168(1)(o), which the Central Bank's board decides. The Grievances Committee hears challenges; it does not impose sanctions.

cards.title: How a sanction works (Article 168)
cards.body:
**Who can be sanctioned:** a licensed institution, an Authorized Individual, or anyone carrying on licensed activities without a licence, for breaching the law, Central Bank rules or measures, including AML/CFT measures.

**Selected sanctions**
- Fine on an institution up to **AED 1,000,000,000** (168(1)(m)).
- Fine up to **ten times** the funds involved or unjust enrichment (168(1)(l)).
- Fine on an Authorized Individual of **AED 100,000 to 5,000,000** (168(1)(q)).
- Fine of at least **AED 1,000,000** for unlicensed activity or an unauthorized Designated Function (168(1)(s)).
- Return of funds to customers, with any excess going to the Central Bank (168(1)(k)).

**Procedure**
- Reasoned notice within **15 working days**, stating the grievance right (168(3)).
- Sanctions are **immediately enforceable**; fines can be debited automatically from the violator's accounts (168(4)).
- The Central Bank may settle fines by reconciliation (168(6)) and may **publish** decisions naming the violator (168(7)).

cards.title: Administrative sanction or criminal penalty?
cards.prompt: Sort each consequence by its source in the 2025 law.

items.text: A caution issued by the Central Bank
An order to return funds to customers
Removal of an Authorized Individual
A fine of up to AED 1bn on the institution
Imprisonment for obstructing an examination
At least one year's imprisonment for performing a Designated Function without authorization
Imprisonment and/or a fine for intentionally disclosing customer data
Imprisonment and/or a fine of AED 50,000 to 500m for unlicensed activity

lines.text: One of my team wants to delete some draft notes from last year's fraud log. He says they are 'just speculation' and might confuse the examiners.
Stop him. Article 179 makes it a crime to destroy, mutilate or alter documents relating to a matter under Central Bank examination.
It also covers obstructing or delaying the examination, or concealing facts. Complicity counts too.
So we hand over the notes as they are and explain the context?
Exactly. Context is welcome. Editing the record is not.

cards.title: The fraud log
cards.situation: During the examination, an Operations manager proposes deleting draft notes from last year's fraud log and replacing them with a cleaner summary before the examiners see it. The notes show staff suspected a control weakness months before a major incident.

choices.text: Preserve the log unchanged, hand it over as requested, add a written explanation of what the notes show and what was fixed, and remind staff of Article 179
choices.outcome: Best answer. Article 133 requires timely provision of all records on the examination's subject, and Article 179 makes destroying or altering such documents, concealment and complicity crimes. Explaining context is legitimate; editing the record is not.

choices.text: Replace the notes with a clean summary, because the summary is more accurate
choices.outcome: Poor. Altering documents that relate to a matter under examination is a crime under Article 179(3), whatever the motive.

choices.text: Keep the notes but hold them back unless examiners ask for them by name
choices.outcome: Poor. Article 133(4) requires all information relating to the subject of the examination on a timely basis. Holding back relevant records risks concealment and obstruction under Article 179.

choices.text: Hand over the notes but tell staff not to discuss them if examiners ask
choices.outcome: Partly right. The record is preserved, but discouraging staff from answering could delay or obstruct the examination. Examiners may summon any related person under Article 133(5).

items.label: Decision issued
items.detail: For example, a sanction under Article 168 or a licence restriction under Article 65.

items.label: Reasoned notice
items.detail: Sanction decisions must be notified with reasons and the grievance right (Article 168(3)).

items.label: Grievance filed
items.detail: File with the Grievances and Appeals Committee within 20 working days of notice or proven knowledge (Article 167(10)).

items.label: Grievance decided
items.detail: The committee may suspend the decision meanwhile, and may fine up to AED 100,000 if it rejects the grievance (Article 167(8)-(9)).

items.label: Higher Federal Court
items.detail: The committee's decision is final and can be challenged only before the Higher Federal Court within 20 working days (Article 167(6)).

cards.front: When can early intervention start?
cards.back: When a bank breaches, or is likely to breach, capital or liquidity requirements because its finances are deteriorating fast, or its financial position is deficient (142(1)).

cards.front: Name three early intervention measures
cards.back: Apply the recovery plan, add capital, impose extra liquidity requirements, change strategy or structure, or replace unfit directors (142(1)).

cards.front: Who is the UAE's resolution authority?
cards.back: The Central Bank (Article 143(1)).

cards.front: Name two resolution powers
cards.back: Bail-in, a bridge institution, an asset management vehicle, transfer to a buyer, or claw-back of pay from responsible persons (143(1)).

cards.front: In resolution, who ranks just after secured creditors?
cards.back: Unpaid staff pay for the six months before resolution starts (Article 144(2)).

cards.front: What if someone ignores early intervention instructions?
cards.back: Imprisonment and/or a fine of AED 100,000 to 10 million (Article 176).

cards.title: Getting examination-ready
cards.prompt: Put Dunecrest's examination readiness steps in a sensible order.
steps: Map each article of the 2025 law to an owner, policy and control
Check authorizations for every Designated Function and the related approvals
Test reporting: qualified staff, data access, reconciliations and sign-offs
Review complaints, compound interest and fraud handling against Articles 147-150
Assemble the evidence file and brief staff on Articles 133 and 179
Track findings to closure and report progress to the board

cards.question: A Dunecrest violation was committed by employees acting in the bank's name. Which statement matches Article 181?
options: Only the employees who acted are liable, never their managers
Only the bank is liable, because a company acts through its board
The manager in charge can face the same penalties if he knew of it or it resulted from his negligence, and the bank is jointly liable for fines
The manager is liable only if he personally gained from the violation
cards.explanation: Article 181(1) applies the same penalties to the official in charge of management when he knew of the violation or it resulted from his negligence or failure to perform his duties, and 181(2) makes the legal person jointly liable for fines and damages for violations by its employees in its name.

cards.title: Dunecrest's readiness file (fictional)
cards.body:
Before the examiners leave, Layla presents the file the board approved after the gap analysis:

- **Law map:** every relevant article, its owner and the policy or control that meets it.
- **People:** register of Designated Functions with Central Bank authorization dates and limits (Arts 107-112, 130).
- **Reporting:** the qualified-staff standard, training records, return calendar, reconciliations and sign-offs (Arts 116, 122-124).
- **Customers:** complaint decisions with written reasons, the compound interest remediation, fraud incidents and customer notices (Arts 147-150).
- **Escalation log:** Matters of Significance and violations reported under Article 123.
- **Transition:** how the bank aligned within the Article 184 period and which surviving regulations it still applies under Article 183.

The examiners still raise findings, but they can trace each one to an owner and a fix date.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: The Central Bank can examine at any time, demand records promptly and summon people; obstruction, concealment and altering documents are crimes (Articles 133, 179).
Article 168 sanctions run from a caution to AED 1bn fines, removal of Authorized Individuals and licence revocation, and are immediately enforceable.
Challenge decisions before the Grievances and Appeals Committee within 20 working days, then the Higher Federal Court within 20 working days (Article 167).
Managers in charge can be personally punished for violations they knew of or caused by negligence (Article 181).
Early intervention and resolution powers (Articles 142-144) make recovery planning and sound governance a board-level priority.

cards.prompt: If the Central Bank examined your area next week, which record would you be least comfortable handing over, and what would make it ready?

quiz.question: When may the Central Bank send examiners to Dunecrest under Article 133?
options: Only with the approval of Dunecrest's board
At any time it considers necessary to check soundness and compliance
Only after a customer complaint is filed
Only once a year after giving 30 days' notice
quiz.explanation: Article 133(1) lets the Central Bank send its staff or an authorized third party at any time it deems necessary to check soundness and compliance. No notice period, complaint or board approval is required.

quiz.question: What is the maximum fine Article 168 allows the Central Bank to impose on a licensed institution?
options: Ten million dirhams
Five hundred million dirhams
One hundred million dirhams
One billion dirhams
quiz.explanation: Article 168(1)(m) allows a fine not exceeding AED 1,000,000,000 on a violating institution. Other figures appear elsewhere in the law, for example AED 500m as the top criminal fine for unlicensed activity in Article 170.

quiz.question: An Authorized Individual at Dunecrest repeatedly signs off returns he knows to be wrong. Which Article 168 sanctions could apply to him personally?
options: Only a caution, because Article 168 allows fines on institutions but never on individuals
Only a ban on travel outside the UAE
An AED 100,000-5m fine and a ban on any function at any licensed institution
Only a deduction from the bank's dividends
quiz.explanation: Article 168(1)(q) and (r) allow a fine of AED 100,000 to 5 million on a violating Authorized Individual and a ban on any function at his institution or any other licensed institution. Criminal penalties under Article 179 may also apply.

quiz.question: Within what period must the violator be officially notified of a reasoned sanction decision?
options: Within sixty working days of its issue
Within one year of the violation
Within fifteen working days of its issue
Within three months of the examination
quiz.explanation: Article 168(3) requires reasoned notice within fifteen working days, stating the content, reasons, effective date and grievance right. Twenty working days is the period used for most other notices in the law.

quiz.question: Dunecrest receives a sanction notice and wants to contest it. Where and by when must it file?
options: With the Grievances and Appeals Committee, within twenty working days
With the Central Bank's board, within sixty days
With the Ministry of Finance, within three months
With the Court of Appeal, within thirty days of notification, as for any customer dispute
quiz.explanation: Article 167(10) bars grievances filed more than twenty working days after notification or proven knowledge, and 167(5) gives the committee exclusive jurisdiction over most Central Bank decisions. The Court of Appeal route belongs to customer disputes over AED 100,000.

quiz.question: Can Dunecrest challenge a general Central Bank regulation, such as a new reporting standard, before the Grievances and Appeals Committee?
options: Yes, but only with the support of other banks
No, but the Higher Federal Court hears such challenges first
Yes, any Central Bank document, including a general regulation, can be grieved within 20 working days
No. General regulations and instructions are outside the committee's jurisdiction
quiz.explanation: Article 167(5) gives the committee exclusive jurisdiction over Central Bank decisions, procedures and measures, except regulations, directives, instructions, policies and regulatory and supervisory decisions of a general nature.

quiz.question: During an examination, a manager delays handing over requested loan files for weeks without reason. Which offence is he most exposed to?
options: Mutilating currency under Article 173
Obstructing or delaying an examination, punishable under Article 179
Issuing currency under Article 172
Using the word 'bank' without a licence under Article 177
quiz.explanation: Article 179(4) punishes whoever obstructs, resists or delays a Central Bank examination or the provision of information, with imprisonment and/or a fine of at least AED 500,000. The other articles concern unrelated offences.

quiz.question: Which measure may the Central Bank take under Article 133(7) when an examination finds a violation?
options: Replace the bank's external auditor with a Central Bank employee for the rest of the financial year
Appoint an expert or qualified Central Bank employee to oversee some operations
Sell the bank's shares on the market without notice
Transfer the bank's customers to another bank immediately
quiz.explanation: Article 133(7)(c) allows appointing an expert or qualified Central Bank employee to advise, supervise or oversee operations for a set period, at the bank's cost for an outside expert. The other actions are not Article 133 measures.

quiz.question: Dunecrest is likely to breach its capital requirement as its finances deteriorate quickly. Which is an early intervention measure under Article 142?
options: Requiring Dunecrest to stop filing regulatory returns
Requiring Dunecrest to implement measures from its recovery plan
Requiring Dunecrest to open new branches to raise income
Requiring Dunecrest to double its dividend payout
quiz.explanation: Article 142(1)(a) lets the Central Bank require the institution to implement one or more measures in its recovery plan. Raising dividends, expanding branches or stopping returns would not address the problem and are not listed.

quiz.question: A company commits a violation of the 2025 law through its staff, and the general manager knew about it. What does Article 181 provide?
options: The manager can receive the same penalties, and the company is jointly liable for fines
The manager is punished only if the company is closed down or declared bankrupt as a result of the violation
Only the company is punished, never its managers
The staff are punished and the company is exempt
quiz.explanation: Article 181(1) applies the same penalties to the official in charge of management when he knew of the violation or it resulted from his negligence, and 181(2) makes the company jointly liable for fines and damages where employees acted in its name.

regulators: Grievances and Appeals Committee (Federal Decree-Law No. 6 of 2025, Article 167)

bank.question: Dunecrest's board asks which Central Bank function in Article 5(2) most directly supports the bank's duty to keep staff competent. Which is it?
options: Monitoring and analysing systemic risk across the financial system, including individual staff errors
Maintaining foreign reserves to cover the monetary base
Issuing rules so licensed activities run with integrity, prudence and competence
Designing the Dirham's exchange rate regime with Cabinet approval
bank.explanation: Article 5(2)(c) ties Central Bank rules to integrity, prudence and appropriate professional competence in licensed activities. Reserves, exchange rate policy and systemic risk monitoring are real functions but are not about staff competence.

bank.question: An internal memo says 'the 2018 law's regulations died with it, so we only follow rules issued after September 2025'. What is the main legal error?
options: Article 132 makes post-2025 regulations apply backwards to 2018
Article 185 repealed only the 2023 insurance law, so the 2018 Central Bank law still applies in full today
Article 2 limits the new law to institutions licensed after 2025
Article 183 keeps regulations made under the 2018 law in force until replaced
bank.explanation: Article 185 repealed the 2018 law, but Article 183 preserves the regulations, standards and circulars made under it until replaced. Article 132 says rules are not retroactive, and Article 2 sets geographic scope, not licence dates.

bank.question: Two years after the law took effect, an examiner finds Dunecrest never updated a policy that conflicts with the new law. Dunecrest argues it is 'still within the transition'. What is the strongest response?
options: Article 183 gives unlimited time to align as long as any regulation made under the 2018 law remains in force
Article 188 delays the law until the next Rulebook update
Article 132 lets banks keep any policy agreed before the law
The one-year period in Article 184 has ended unless the board extended it
bank.explanation: Article 184 required alignment within one year of entry into force, extendable only by the board. Article 183 keeps old regulations alive but does not suspend the new law's own requirements, Article 132 protects customer agreements not internal policies, and Article 188 brought the law into force the day after publication.

bank.question: Which pair correctly matches a Central Bank objective with the article that sets it?
options: Prudent management of foreign reserves, Article 5(1)
Supervising free zone banks, Article 2
Promoting sustainable finance as an objective, Article 3
Setting bank lending rates for customers, Article 5(1)
bank.explanation: Prudent reserve management is one of the three objectives in Article 5(1). Sustainable finance appears as a function in Article 5(2)(e), not an objective in Article 3. Article 5 does not set customer lending rates, and Article 2 excludes free zone institutions.

bank.question: The Central Bank wants industry views on a draft rule for licensed institutions. Which statement reflects Article 30?
options: It may invite public or industry comments within a set period and publish them
It must hold a public hearing before every new regulation
It must obtain the written consent of the banks' association before issuing any rule that affects banks
It may consult only other regulators, never the public
bank.explanation: Article 30 lets the Central Bank choose to involve the public or industry professionals within a set period and to publish comments for transparency. Consultation is optional, and no consent or hearing requirement appears.

bank.question: A customer offers to settle a AED 120 bill entirely in 50-fils coins at a branch. Which statement about coins under Article 54 is right?
options: Coins are legal tender only at the Central Bank's own branches and not between private parties or banks
Coins are legal tender for any amount, like notes
Coins are legal tender only up to AED 50, though the Central Bank accepts any amount
Coins are no longer legal tender once digital currency exists
bank.explanation: Article 54(2) makes coins legal tender for payments not exceeding fifty dirhams, while the Central Bank accepts any amount presented to it. Notes and digital currency are legal tender for any amount under Article 54(1).

bank.question: Which Central Bank power under Article 35 could most directly lead to extra requirements on a large bank like Dunecrest?
options: Appointing its external auditor without giving reasons
Setting its share price on the stock market
Designating it as a systemically important institution and requiring it to take necessary measures
Approving its annual staff salary increases
bank.explanation: Article 35 gives the Central Bank sole authority to designate a licensed institution as systemically important and to require measures from it. Auditor appointment is covered by Article 140 only when a bank fails to appoint one, and share prices and salaries are not Central Bank decisions.

bank.question: Which source should a Dunecrest analyst treat as the official home of all Central Bank regulations today?
options: Press coverage of Central Bank announcements
The previous year's internal compliance manual
The Central Bank's electronic Rulebook on its official website
The Ministry of Finance's FAQ pages
bank.explanation: Article 131 requires the Central Bank to publish and regularly update an electronic guide of all its regulations on its website. Ministry pages, press coverage and internal manuals are useful but are not the official, complete source.

bank.question: A fintech offers Dunecrest customers instant transfers through its own app using Dunecrest's brand, without its own licence. Which provisions should Compliance test first?
options: Article 147 on confidentiality and Article 150 on credit guarantees
Article 116 on related-party statements and Article 129 on single-borrower lending limits for the partner
Article 46 on reserve cover and Article 52 on the currency unit
Articles 60, 61(1)(h) and 62 on unlicensed activity, promotion, marketing and technology
bank.explanation: The risk is that the fintech carries on or promotes a licensed activity without a licence. Articles 60, 61(1)(h) and 62 address exactly that, whatever technology is used. The other articles cover unrelated duties.

bank.question: Dunecrest's licence lists certain activities. A business unit starts acting as principal in commodity derivatives, which the licence does not cover. What is the legal position?
options: It is lawful, because all banks may trade derivatives by default
It breaches the licence-scope duty and can attract criminal penalties
It is lawful, because acting as principal in derivatives is not one of the activities the law lists
It is lawful, provided the trades are reported quarterly
bank.explanation: Article 60(6) requires business within the licence scope, and Article 61(1)(i) lists acting as principal in financial products such as derivatives and commodities as a licensed activity. Article 174(1) punishes breach of Article 60(6) with imprisonment and/or a fine of AED 200,000 to 10 million.

bank.question: Which statement about the register of licensed financial institutions is correct?
options: The register is internal to the Central Bank and never published
Entry happens automatically one year after licensing
Entry is optional for banks licensed before 2025
An institution may not start any licensed activity until its name is entered on the register
bank.explanation: Article 68 creates an electronic register published on the Central Bank's website and says no licensed activity may begin before the name is entered. It is neither secret nor optional.

bank.question: The Central Bank wants to add a restriction to Dunecrest's licence. Which procedural rights does Article 65 give Dunecrest?
options: It may delay the restriction until the next general assembly
It has no rights at all, because licence conditions are general regulations that cannot be grieved
It must consent in writing before any restriction applies
It may be asked to comment first and must get a reasoned notice within 20 working days
bank.explanation: Article 65 lets the Central Bank ask for the institution's comments before deciding and requires official notice within twenty working days stating content, reasons, effective date and the right to grieve. No consent is needed.

bank.question: Which of the following is NOT listed in Article 66 as a ground for suspending or revoking a licence?
options: Ceasing a licensed activity for more than one year
Staff refusing to cooperate with Central Bank examiners
Capital falling below the required minimum
The institution reporting a quarterly loss
bank.explanation: Article 66(1) lists, among others, refusal to cooperate with examiners (n), ceasing an activity for over a year (d) and capital below the minimum (k). A single quarterly loss is not a listed ground.

bank.question: Dunecrest's board wants to renew a director's board term. A minority shareholder says the general assembly decides alone. What does Article 130 add?
options: The Central Bank must be informed within thirty days after the vote
The Central Bank must approve the renewal in advance and may reject it
The renewal needs Central Bank approval only if the director is also the chief executive of the bank
Nothing, because director renewals are purely a shareholder matter
bank.explanation: Article 130(2) requires prior Central Bank approval for nominating, appointing or renewing board members, and Article 130(3) lets the Central Bank's board reject them to safeguard the public interest.

bank.question: The Central Bank rejects Dunecrest's application to authorize a new chief executive. What can Dunecrest do?
options: Ask the general assembly to overrule the Central Bank
Appoint the person on an interim basis while it reapplies
File a grievance with the Grievances and Appeals Committee, as the rejection notice must state
Nothing, because authorization decisions are final
bank.explanation: Article 109(3) requires the rejection notice to include the right to file a grievance with the Grievances and Appeals Committee. Interim appointment would breach Article 107, and shareholders cannot overrule the Central Bank.

bank.question: Which situation would allow the Central Bank to bar an individual from working in licensed financial activities under Article 112?
options: The individual has worked at the bank for less than one year
The individual holds shares in a listed company
The individual has resigned from a competitor bank
It considers that the individual is not fit and proper to work or perform Designated Functions
bank.explanation: Article 112(1) allows the Central Bank to prohibit an individual from working in or performing Designated Functions related to licensed activities if it considers them not fit and proper. Tenure, prior employers and shareholdings are not grounds in themselves.

bank.question: An investor plans to buy a stake that would give it de facto control of Dunecrest, without telling the Central Bank. Which measure could the Central Bank impose if it proceeds?
options: Ordering the stake sold and suspending the investor's voting and dividend rights
Requiring Dunecrest to delist from the stock market
Cancelling Dunecrest's licence immediately and without notice, because the bank allowed the purchase
Fining the investor's customers for funding the purchase
bank.explanation: Article 120 requires prior approval to hold or increase a controlling interest and lists measures for breaches, including ordering the sale, depriving dividends and preventing voting or board candidacy. Immediate licence cancellation, fines on customers and delisting are not listed.

bank.question: A police officer emails a branch asking for a customer's statements 'for an informal check', citing no legal power. What is the best response?
options: Route the request to Legal or Compliance to confirm a legal basis before any disclosure
Refuse permanently, because Article 147 has no exceptions
Send the statements immediately, because the police always have power
Tell the customer and ask him to deal with the police directly
bank.explanation: Article 147(6)(a) preserves powers legally vested in security and judicial authorities, so disclosure may be lawful, but only where such a power is actually being exercised. Confirming the legal basis protects both the customer and the bank. Sending the officer to the customer does not answer whether a legal power exists.

bank.question: Dunecrest is acquiring another bank's card portfolio with Central Bank approval. Can customer data move with the portfolio?
options: No, each customer must consent individually first
Yes, Article 147(6)(f) covers a Central Bank-approved transfer or acquisition
Yes, but only after the acquisition completes and all of the customer data has been fully anonymised
No, data can move only through a court order
bank.explanation: Article 147(6)(f) lets institutions transfer customer data to establish their rights in a transfer of business, merger or acquisition approved by the Central Bank. Individual consent or a court order is not required for that exception.

bank.question: An outside consultant migrating Dunecrest's core banking system can see customer balances. Is he bound by the confidentiality duty?
options: Only for data he copies onto his own devices
Yes. Article 147 binds consultants and anyone with access through their work
No. Only employees on the bank's own payroll are bound by Article 147, not outside contractors
Only if he has signed a separate non-disclosure agreement
bank.explanation: Article 147(3) names experts, consultants and technicians assigned to work in the institution, and 147(4) extends the ban to anyone able to access the data through their profession, position or work. An NDA is good practice but not the source of the duty.

bank.question: A dispute committee awards a customer AED 250,000 against Dunecrest. Dunecrest wants to contest it. What is the route and deadline?
options: Challenge before the Court of Appeal within 30 days
Grievance to the Grievances and Appeals Committee within 20 working days
No challenge is possible, because all resolutions are final
Appeal to the Higher Federal Court within 20 working days
bank.explanation: Article 148(7) lets either party challenge resolutions on disputes above AED 100,000 before the competent Court of Appeal within 30 days, after which a challenge is inadmissible. The Grievances Committee handles Central Bank decisions, not customer disputes.

bank.question: Dunecrest's card team learns from another bank that a merchant is running a skimming scheme. The Central Bank later asks for Dunecrest's fraud patterns and mitigation data. What must Dunecrest do?
options: Provide the data only if the other bank agrees first
Decline until the police investigation is complete
Provide only aggregated numbers, because fraud data about customers is confidential under Article 147
Provide the data, cooperate fully and apply preventive measures on time
bank.explanation: Article 149(4) lets the Central Bank require data, transaction records, fraud patterns and mitigation measures, and 149(5) requires full cooperation and implementation of preventive measures within its deadlines. Confidentiality does not override the Central Bank's powers (147(6)(a)).

bank.question: A product team argues that a fee is lawful because it is disclosed on page 34 of the terms. Which duty is most at risk?
options: Publishing audited accounts in every branch (Article 141)
Providing clear, transparent and easily accessible information on fees, terms and risks (Article 149(7))
Obtaining prior approval for new branches (Article 121)
Maintaining reserve requirements with the Central Bank (Article 32)
bank.explanation: Article 149(7) requires clear, transparent and easily accessible fee, term and risk information so customers can decide in an informed way. A fee buried deep in long terms is unlikely to meet that standard. The other duties are unrelated.

bank.question: Collections staff propose to capitalise overdue interest on a corporate customer's overdraft. What should Compliance advise?
options: The ban covers facilities to customers generally, so the plan conflicts with Article 148(11)
The ban applies only to loans above AED 100,000
The ban applies only once the Central Bank issues a circular
The ban protects only individual consumers, so overdrafts to corporate customers are not affected by it
bank.explanation: Article 148(11) refers to facilities extended to customers without limiting it to individuals or to any value, and requires institutions to follow the Central Bank's rules on applying it. The prohibition itself is already in the law.

bank.question: Which statement about the Central Bank's independent complaints unit is supported by Article 148?
options: It only gives non-binding advice and cannot decide disputes
It hears only complaints worth more than AED 100,000
It has legal personality, issues binding resolutions and its committees are judge-led
It is a complaints department inside each bank that reports to that bank's own board of directors
bank.explanation: Article 148(2) establishes an independent unit with legal personality to decide complaints with binding resolutions, and 148(5) has its committees headed by a judge with another judge and experts. It is not part of any bank and has no minimum claim value.

bank.question: An examiner asks Dunecrest to show how it meets Article 122(1)(b). Which evidence is strongest?
options: A letter from the external auditor praising the finance team
Role profiles, qualification and training records for reporting staff, and documented review of each return
The reporting team's annual leave schedule
The total number of returns filed during the year
bank.explanation: Article 122(1)(b) requires qualified employees assigned to prepare reports, so evidence of qualification, assignment and review is most relevant. An auditor's letter and filing counts do not show that the preparers are qualified.

bank.question: Dunecrest's reporting manager files a return containing a figure she knows is incomplete, to meet the deadline, without any note. What is her personal exposure?
options: Only an internal performance warning from her manager
Central Bank measures under Article 122(6) and criminal penalties under Article 179
Only a fine on the bank, which cannot be passed to staff
None, because the duty to report rests only on the institution and never on individual employees
bank.explanation: Article 122(6) lets the Central Bank take measures against the assigned employees, and Article 179(1) punishes whoever provides misleading or incomplete information to the Central Bank with imprisonment and/or a fine of at least AED 500,000.

bank.question: The Central Bank reviews Dunecrest's audit report and finds a shortfall in provisions. What may it do under Article 140(2), and when?
options: Within twenty working days, order a new general assembly vote on the accounts and the auditor's appointment
Within three months, replace the bank's external auditor
Within ten working days, refuse to approve the proposed profit distribution
At any time, cancel the bank's licence automatically
bank.explanation: Article 140(2) allows the Central Bank, within ten working days of receiving the report, to refuse to approve proposed profit distribution where it finds a provisions shortfall, a capital adequacy decline or relevant reservations.

bank.question: Dunecrest's external auditor offers to take a mortgage from Dunecrest at staff rates. What does Article 140 say?
options: A licensed institution may not extend credit facilities of any type to its auditors
It is allowed if the audit partner is not the borrower
It is allowed if priced at market rates
It is allowed if disclosed in the annual report
bank.explanation: Article 140(5) bans credit facilities of any type to the institution's auditors and requires an approved auditor to settle obligations to the institution before starting. Pricing or disclosure does not cure it.

bank.question: Which matter would most clearly fall under the immediate reporting duty in Article 123 rather than routine periodic returns?
options: Month-end balances that are within all limits
Discovering that the bank has breached a Central Bank regulation on large exposures
A routine staff promotion in Operations
A planned change to branch opening hours
bank.explanation: Article 123(1)(b) requires immediate reporting of any violation of the law or of Central Bank regulations and instructions, and 123(1)(a) of Matters of Significance. Routine balances, opening hours and ordinary promotions are not such matters.

bank.question: A business unit repeatedly delivers source data two days after the reporting deadline. Whose duty is it under the law to fix this?
options: The external auditor's, by estimating the missing data
The Central Bank's, by extending all deadlines
The bank's, under Article 122(1)(c)
The reporting analyst's alone, by working weekends
bank.explanation: Article 122(1)(c) puts the duty on the licensed institution to take appropriate measures so assigned employees get the information required. Persistent late data is a governance failure to escalate, not a burden for analysts or auditors.

bank.question: Dunecrest is a branch of a foreign bank incorporated outside the UAE. What must it do with its auditors' report under Article 140(3)?
options: Send it to the Central Bank within three months of year end only, with no copy needed for head office
Publish it only in the home country's newspapers
Send it to head office and to the Central Bank within 20 working days of issue
Keep it at the branch for examiners on request
bank.explanation: Article 140(3) requires institutions incorporated outside the State to forward the auditors' report to head office and to submit a copy to the Central Bank within 20 working days of its issue. Article 139 also requires separate UAE accounts for foreign branches.

bank.question: The Central Bank asks Dunecrest's auditors for a report on the bank's compliance with the 2025 law. Who pays?
options: Dunecrest, because Article 140(7) puts the cost on the licensed institution
The shareholders directly, by special levy
The auditors, as part of their professional duty
The Central Bank, as part of its supervision budget
bank.explanation: Article 140(7) lets the Central Bank require auditors to report on the institution's compliance, at the institution's expense. The Central Bank and auditors do not bear that cost.

bank.question: Dunecrest's head of reporting is asked by the chief executive to agree informally that 'sensitive items' will be routed through him before reaching the Central Bank, with no time limit. Which response is best?
options: Agree, because the chief executive is an Authorized Individual and is personally accountable for every return
Agree, if the arrangement is written into a policy
Decline, because Article 122(2) bans such an arrangement, and escalate to Compliance
Agree, but copy the external auditor on each item
bank.explanation: Article 122(2) prohibits instructions or agreements with any manager, officer or employee to decline to provide the Central Bank with what it requires. Seniority and formal policies do not make such an arrangement lawful.

bank.question: A Central Bank sanction fines Dunecrest. Dunecrest files a grievance and argues it need not pay until the committee decides. What is the correct position?
options: The fine is payable only after the Higher Federal Court has ruled on any further challenge by the bank
They are immediately enforceable unless the committee suspends the decision
The fine is payable only if the general assembly agrees
Filing a grievance automatically suspends every sanction
bank.explanation: Article 168(4) makes administrative sanctions immediately enforceable, with fines debited from the violator's accounts, and Article 167(9) lets the committee suspend the decision if it deems it necessary. Filing alone does not suspend.

bank.question: Dunecrest overcharged 4,000 customers by AED 2m in breach of Central Bank rules. Which combination of Article 168 sanctions fits the facts most directly?
options: A suspension of the customers' accounts until repayment
A reduction in the Central Bank's paid-up capital
A ban on the bank using the word 'bank' and a currency fine
An order to return the funds to customers plus a fine of up to ten times the amount involved
bank.explanation: Article 168(1)(k) lets the Central Bank require the violator to return funds obtained through the violation to customers, and 168(1)(l) allows a fine of up to ten times the funds involved. The other options are not Article 168 sanctions.

bank.question: The Grievances and Appeals Committee rejects Dunecrest's grievance and also fines it for bringing it. What is the maximum fine, and what route remains?
options: Up to AED 100,000, then the Higher Federal Court within 20 working days
Up to AED 500,000, and no further challenge at all
Up to AED 1m, and then a challenge before the competent Court of Appeal within 30 days
Up to AED 100,000, and a new grievance to the same committee
bank.explanation: Article 167(8) allows a fine up to AED 100,000 when the committee rejects or does not accept a grievance, and 167(6) allows a challenge only before the Higher Federal Court within 20 working days of notification.

bank.question: The Central Bank decides to publish a sanction against Dunecrest on its website, naming the bank. Is that allowed?
options: Yes. Article 168(7) allows publishing decisions that name violators
Only if Dunecrest consents to publication
Only after the Higher Federal Court confirms the sanction
No. Article 147 makes all supervisory decisions about a bank confidential, just like customer data
bank.explanation: Article 168(7) lets the Central Bank publish decisions about any violating person on its website, including the name, under the board's controls. Article 147 protects customer data, not sanction decisions about institutions.

bank.question: Dunecrest is placed in resolution. Which group is paid first after holders of secured debts, under Article 144?
options: The Central Bank's general reserve
Staff pay accrued and unpaid for the six months before resolution
All unsecured bond holders, ranked equally with depositors and other customers of the bank
Shareholders of the bank
bank.explanation: Article 144 ranks secured creditors first, then unpaid staff pay for the six months before resolution, then reasonable resolution costs, then customers, then other creditors, and shareholders last.

bank.question: Which power does the Central Bank have only as resolution authority under Article 143, rather than as an early intervention measure under Article 142?
options: Imposing additional liquidity requirements
Carrying out a bail-in or establishing a bridge institution
Requiring the bank to apply its recovery plan
Requiring changes to the bank's business strategy
bank.explanation: Bail-in and a bridge institution are resolution powers in Article 143(1)(h) and (j). The recovery plan, strategy changes and extra liquidity are early intervention measures in Article 142(1).

bank.question: Dunecrest's chief executive learned of a reporting violation by his team and did nothing. The violation is later prosecuted under Article 179. What is his personal exposure?
options: None, because Article 179 applies only to the employees who filed
Only a Central Bank caution addressed to the bank
Only removal from the board, never a fine
He can receive the same penalties under Article 181
bank.explanation: Article 181(1) applies the penalties for violations committed by a legal person to the official in charge of management whenever his knowledge is established or the violation resulted from his negligence. Article 179 carries imprisonment and/or a fine of at least AED 500,000.

bank.question: Which item would best demonstrate to examiners that Dunecrest applied Articles 183 and 184 properly?
options: A board-approved gap analysis of alignment and surviving rules
A press release welcoming the new law
Minutes showing the board noted the new law without further action
A list of all regulations issued under the 2018 law, marked 'repealed'
bank.explanation: Article 184 required alignment within one year (unless extended), and Article 183 keeps earlier regulations in force until replaced. A gap analysis shows both. Marking all old regulations as repealed misreads Article 183, and noting the law without action shows no alignment.
